tagline: Napoleon to Wellington by way of Waterloo, along the river.
intro: Route 224 is the old US 24, the road through the river towns until a bypass took the traffic away in 1959. From the west end it runs through Napoleon and Wellington beside the Missouri, close enough to be prone to flooding, and comes into Lexington on the bluffs.
The two little towns were laid out in 1836 and 1837 and named for the commanders at Waterloo. Lexington grew rich on hemp, tobacco and cattle, and in September 1861 the hemp went to war.

moments.title: Waterloo
moments.text: About halfway between Napoleon and Wellington lies a small unincorporated crossroads that could hardly have been called anything else.

moments.title: Battle of the Hemp Bales
moments.text: Here Price's Missouri State Guard rolled river-soaked hemp bales up the bluff as a moving breastwork in 1861, and the red-hot shot fired at them would not take.

moments.title: Lexington
moments.text: A cannonball from the siege sits in an upper pillar of the 1847 courthouse, though by accounts from 1920 it fell out and was screwed onto a two-foot iron rod decades later.
